dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 style with LINE SEQUENTIAL organization; likely compiled with GnuCOBOL given relative file paths and no vendor-specific extensions
evidence: GOBACK at end of main paragraph

purpose.domain_detail: Student project (Final Project by Raje Singh, 2021) for a retail/commerce data processing course
purpose.summary: Reads a file of validated transaction records and splits them into two output files: one for sales and layaway records, one for returns. Produces a summary report with counts, amounts, per-store totals, per-payment-type percentages, and a grand total.

notable_features: SEARCH with VARYING and SET for array lookup
OCCURS with INDEXED BY on working-storage items
88-level condition names for transaction code classification
REDEFINES used to overlay store/pay-type literal arrays
Inline PERFORM VARYING loops for report generation
No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS
verdict.notes: Author and date-written fields confirm this is a student final project (Raje Singh, 2021-04-14). Relative file paths (../../../../datafiles/...) are consistent with a local development/course environment. No vendor-specific extensions detected; dialect assigned gnucobol as most likely open-source compiler used in academic settings, but could be any standard COBOL-85 compiler.
